newsitem.title: USA: Domenici suggests two-step process on Medicare.
newsitem.headline: Domenici suggests two-step process on Medicare.

text.p: Republican Sen. Pete Domenici said on Sunday the White House and Congress should agree on what is needed to make Medicare solvent for the next ten years and leave its health over the next 50 years to a commission.
Reforming Medicare, a federally funded programe that provides health care to the elderly, is seen as a key element of balancing the U.S. federal budget.

"The White House and Congress ought to agree on what is the dollar savings necessary to make it solvent for our seniors for ten years," Domenici told CNN's Late Edition. "Then you can put in a commission to look at it for 50 years.

"I think the president can get that done and Congress will come right along and we will fix that program," added the New Mexico Republican, who chairs the Senate Budget Committee. "When you fix it, you help the budget."
